API

Plugin API reference

Every member of the plugin API with its signature, straight from the types the Code tab uses. For how the parts fit together, read the Plugin API guide first.

api

What register(api) gets. Everything else on this page hangs off it.

PluginApi

MemberSignature and what it does
api.versionreadonly version: string
PLUGIN_API_VERSION
api.threereadonly three: typeof THREE
api.preadonly p: ParamBuilders
The parameter builders (API 3.1, p.number({ min, max, slider? }), p.choice(["a", "b"]) …): they write the plain parameter objects, and the register functions infer the handler's params from them
api.registerComponent()registerComponent<const S extends ComponentSpec>(type: string, spec: S, apply: ComponentApply<PluginParams<S>, ActionsOf<S>, EventsOf<S>>): void
A component: its spec (parameters, and optionally actions, events, uses) and apply, which gets the parameters typed from the spec (params.speed: number), emit for the declared events and returns hooks (onAction for the declared actions)
api.registerLayer()registerLayer<const S extends ComponentSpec>(type: string, spec: S, layer: LayerDefinition): void
api.registerNodeType()registerNodeType<const S extends NodeTypeSpec>(type: string, spec: S, build: NodeTypeBuild<PluginParams<S>, ActionsOf<S>, EventsOf<S>>): void
A node type of the plugin's own: build makes its three.js object with api.three (Points, a Sprite, a Line, a mesh with its own material); the engine places it like every node – placement, children, components and layers come with it. The spec declares its parameters (rows in the Entity panel, values in the node's params) and the file its src takes (glb, video, image or none).
api.registerPass()registerPass<const S extends PassSpec>(type: string, spec: S, factory: PassFactory<PluginParams<S>>): void
A post-processing pass of the plugin's own: its spec as the built-in passes have it, the factory builds the three.js pass (PassContext: the resolved parameters, shaderPass, the canvas size). The content names it in passes: [{ type, … }]; the plugin's pass leaves the registry when the plugin is uninstalled.
api.registerMaterial()registerMaterial<const S extends MaterialSpec>(type: string, spec: S, build: MaterialBuild<PluginParams<S>>): void
A whole material: build makes a three.js material – a ShaderMaterial with GLSL of its own, a MeshStandardMaterial with a procedural texture – and may return { material, update, tune, dispose }. A node names it as material: { type, params }; it replaces the material of the node's meshes (a model's, a plane's, a plugin node's), the node's layers still add on top. time in the context is a uniform the engine advances.
api.registerTexture()registerTexture<const S extends TextureSpec>(type: string, spec: S, draw: TextureDraw<ParamsOf<S>>): void
A procedural texture: draw makes a three.js texture (a CanvasTexture, a DataTexture) and may return { texture, update, dispose } to animate it. Any spec's texture parameter takes it by its type – a material's, a layer's, a component's, a node type's.
api.registerAppearance()registerAppearance<const S extends AppearanceSpec>(type: string, spec: S, factory: AppearanceFactory<ParamsOf<S>>): void
A look of the plugin's own: how an entity appears and disappears. The factory runs once per animation with the entity, its anchor, the resolved parameters and the moment (AppearanceContext) and returns { duration, update(visible), dispose? } – visible runs from 0 to 1 on reveal and found, from 1 to 0 on lost. The experience names it by its type in appearance: { reveal, found, lost }, in a built-in look's place.
api.eventsreadonly events: PluginEvents
Core events of the scene (read-only) and scene events of the content
api.varsreadonly vars: PluginVars
Variables in the scopes scene, stage, session and experience
api.progressreadonly progress: PluginProgress
The reader's progress: unlocked, consulted, completion (read-only)
api.scenereadonly scene: PluginScene
The current scene
api.loadText()loadText(url: string): Promise<string>
A text file: a shader of the experience's Library by its URL (the Library shows it; a replace gives a new URL and rewrites it in the sources that name it), or a content path (/assets/content/…). One request per URL however often it is asked for; rejects on an HTTP error. A layer's GLSL is a string at register time – load files where a build runs: a material's build, a pass's factory, a node type's build (set the shader when it arrives, needsUpdate).
api.loadModel()loadModel(url: string): Promise<PluginModel>
A model file (.glb, .gltf): a model of the experience's Library by its URL, or a content path (/assets/content/…) – the value of a model parameter, which the author picks in the editor. One request per URL however often it is asked for; rejects on an HTTP error or a file that is no model. The model is shared by everyone who loads the same file: clone what you change (model.scene.clone(), a geometry's clone()), never dispose it. It loads after the build that asked for it returned – apply it when it arrives, and not at all once the node is disposed.
api.feedback()feedback(options: FeedbackOptions): Feedback
A GPU feedback buffer: fragment runs once per frame into a render target the engine keeps (two, swapped every frame, while it reads its own previous frame – the channel "self", the default iChannel0), before the scene renders, with iTime, iTimeDelta, iFrame, iResolution and iChannel0…3 set. Show texture – or put uniform into a ShaderMaterial's uniforms, it follows every swap. Made in a node's build (a node type's, a component's, a material's) it belongs to the node: it pauses while the node is hidden or its page is not in view, and goes with it. Half-float targets by default, float on request – 8 bits where the device renders into neither (a warning).
api.shadertoy()shadertoy(source: string): string
A Shadertoy pass as feedback's fragment: its mainImage(out vec4, in vec2) source unchanged, called with Shadertoy's fragCoord; iTime, iFrame, iResolution, iChannel0…3 are the buffer's. Throws without mainImage.
api.log()log(...args: unknown[]): void
To the console, prefixed with the plugin's id

Every parameter's texts

MemberSignature and what it does
descriptiondescription: string
label?label?: string

A parameter written by hand

A parameter of a spec (a component's, a material layer's, a pass's, a light's, a plugin node type's, a material's, a procedural texture's): its kind with default and range, a description (the editor's help) and an optional label (schema 2.15, plugin API 1.3) – the few words the editor's row shows. Without a label the row shows the name split into words (paramLabel). A texture (schema 2.17, plugin API 1.4) takes a picture: a file (a Library image or video, a file of the content) or a procedural texture a plugin registers (registerTexture) – its value is a TextureValue (below); the engine hands the plugin's code a three.js texture. A model (schema 2.28, plugin API 1.7) takes a model file: a Library model's URL or a /assets/content/… path (in the content's YAML a .glb / .gltf next to the node, which the content build resolves to its path), "" = none – its value is that string, and the plugin's code loads it with api.loadModel(value). A number's min and max are **hard** limits: the guard and the editor refuse a value outside them, the engine keeps the value it had (a warning). Schema 5.1 (#334, plugin API 3.1): its optional slider [lo, hi] is the **soft** range – the span the editor's control offers first, inside min … max – and integer: true takes whole numbers only (min, max and default whole too). The plugin API's builders (api.p, ./spec-builders.ts) write these objects.

export type ComponentParamSpec = ParamText & ({
  kind: "color";
  default: string;
} | {
  kind: "number";
  default: number;
  min: number;
  max: number;
  step?: number;
  unit?: string;
  slider?: readonly [
    number,
    number
  ];
  integer?: boolean;
} | {
  kind: "choice";
  options: readonly string[];
  default: string;
} | {
  kind: "boolean";
  default: boolean;
} | {
  kind: "string";
  default: string;
} | {
  kind: "texture";
  default: string;
} | {
  kind: "model";
  default: string;
});

SpecLogic – what every spec may declare for the Logic view

What a spec says beyond its parameters (schema 5.1, #334, plugin API 3.1) – what the editor's Logic view draws as ports: - actions: the rule verbs it answers on its node (play, pause, stop, show, hide – SPEC_ACTIONS): a rule's play: <node> reaches the component's onAction("play") beside the node's own clip; - events: the scene events it emits (ended) – through its context's emit, on the bus by name; - uses: what its code hears, emits, reads and sets of the bus and the variables, by name – the Logic view joins it to the rules (it reads the plugin's source only for a plugin that declares nothing). The names are camelCase; an action is one of the node verbs, an event never a core event. An older app ignores the fields.

MemberSignature and what it does
actions?actions?: readonly string[]
events?events?: readonly string[]
uses?uses?: SpecUses

LayerDefinition – registerLayer's third argument

A material layer: the body of a GLSL function vec4 (vec4 rgba, vec2 uv, float time, <the parameters>), run on every pixel of the node's material after its own shading, in linear RGB. The spec's parameters arrive as arguments in their order: number → float, boolean → float (0 / 1), color → vec3, choice → int (the index in its options); string parameters are not passed. time is the seconds since the node was built.

PostPass

A registered pass: three's Pass, optionally with update for new parameter values in place (the editor's live edit). render gets the seconds since the last frame as its fourth argument (an animated grain counts its time with it). A feedback buffer the factory makes (api.feedback) belongs to the pass: it steps while the pass runs and goes with it.

Also has the members of Pass (three.js).

MemberSignature and what it does
update?()update?(params: Record<string, unknown>): void

The AR layer's coverage (its alpha) while the image holds more than the AR layer – the editor's stage, where the desk stands in for the camera picture, or the look-around world and sky under the scene; null while the image is the AR layer alone. A pass that reaches the AR layer only (the grade with reach: ar) limits itself to it with this.
